newsitem.title: USA: USDA LIMITS EXPORT FREIGHT CREDIT FOR ALGERIA.
newsitem.headline: USDA LIMITS EXPORT FREIGHT CREDIT FOR ALGERIA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Friday said it is further limiting the amount of freight costs that it will cover on sales made to Algeria under the fiscal 1997 GSM-102 export credit program.
USDA previously said it would provide limited GSM-102 coverage for freight costs incurred on a C and F or CIF basis on sales to Algeria.
USDA's Commodity Credit Corp "has combined the two previously indicated tallies of sales for which freight coverage is included into a single value," USDA said Friday.
"Effective today, CCC will maintain that single tally of guaranteed sales and when it reaches $41 million, no additional freight coverage will be available," USDA said.
"At present, about $18 million of the indicated $41 million remains available," USDA said.
